subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: After checking every current event-ledger read entry point, does OpenClaw expose an untrusted query shape that needs additional denial-of-service controls?
rationale: The reported primitive is not supported by the observed ACP caller contract, but closing a protected security report or adding defense-in-depth policy requires explicit ownership of the intended trust boundary.

options.title: Close after boundary audit
options.body: Close if all reachable callers use fixed server-owned query shapes and no current-main payload can produce materially unbounded work.

options.title: Define bounded query budgets
options.body: Keep open and specify server-side pagination, row, time, or request-rate limits if a reachable caller can induce excessive ledger work.

recommendation.title: Close after boundary audit
recommendation.body: Close if all reachable callers use fixed server-owned query shapes and no current-main payload can produce materially unbounded work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are credited on the relevant ledger/control-plane history and were explicitly routed into this issue's decision timeline.
